label: Pairing UX and connection lifecycle surface

map.subsystem: Pairing UX and connection lifecycle surface (PairingScreen/PairingViewModel + app-side connection orchestration + BLE runtime-permission flow)

capabilities.name: Pairing route + entry/exit navigation
capabilities.behavior: Route id "pairing", registered in GlycemicGptNavHost and listed in `spokeRoutes` so the bottom nav bar is hidden while it is shown; the screen renders its own content with no TopAppBar. Reached only from Settings → Plugins → pump card: button "Pair Pump" (when unpaired) or "Re-pair" (when paired), both calling `onNavigateToPairing` → `navController.navigate("pairing")`. Exit: `LaunchedEffect(connectionState)` fires `onPaired()` when connectionState becomes CONNECTED, wired to `navController.popBackStack()`. There is no explicit back/close button in the screen body — only the system back gesture. Returning to Settings triggers `LifecycleEventEffect(ON_RESUME) { settingsViewModel.loadState() }`, refreshing paired address, plugin activation and battery-optimization status.
edge_cases: CONNECTED reached while screen not on top still pops the back stack (LaunchedEffect keyed on state).
Pairing screen has no top bar/back affordance; only gesture back.
AUTH_FAILED never navigates away.

capabilities.name: Pairing style dispatch (plugin-driven flow selection)
capabilities.behavior: `PairingProfile(style, advertisedName)` from the active DevicePlugin decides the whole flow. `PairingStyle.CENTRAL_SCAN` (default) → phone scans, lists devices, user taps one, enters a code (Tandem). `PairingStyle.ADVERTISE_AND_WAIT` → phone advertises as `advertisedName`, pump connects to it, no scan/no list/no code (Medtronic; advertisedName = "Mobile 000001"). PumpConnectionAdapter maps `registry.activePumpPlugin` → `plugin.pairingProfile`, defaulting to `PairingProfile()` (CENTRAL_SCAN, advertisedName=null) when no pump plugin is active. Header "Pump Pairing" (headlineMedium) and the paired-status card render above the style branch for both styles. Switching the active plugin in Settings changes the flow live via the StateFlow.
edge_cases: No plugin activated → CENTRAL_SCAN default UI, scan() returns emptyFlow (silent no-op, no error shown).
Screen copy in CENTRAL_SCAN is hard-coded Tandem-specific ("Scan for nearby Tandem pumps") even for a non-Tandem central-scan plugin.

capabilities.name: ConnectionState model and producers
capabilities.behavior: `enum ConnectionState { DISCONNECTED, SCANNING, CONNECTING, AUTHENTICATING, AUTH_FAILED, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING }`. Exposed app-wide as `PumpConnectionManager.connectionState`, produced by `PumpConnectionAdapter` = `registry.activePumpPlugin.flatMapLatest { it?.observeConnectionState() ?: flowOf(DISCONNECTED) }.stateIn(scope, Eagerly, DISCONNECTED)` on a Main.immediate scope. Tandem emits DISCONNECTED/CONNECTING/AUTHENTICATING/AUTH_FAILED/CONNECTED/RECONNECTING (never SCANNING). Medtronic emits SCANNING (advertising-for-discovery), CONNECTING (advertising for a session, and pump-connected-pre-auth), AUTHENTICATING, CONNECTED, RECONNECTING, AUTH_FAILED, DISCONNECTED. Consumers: PairingScreen, HomeScreen status row, BleDebugScreen, PumpConnectionService wake-lock watcher, PumpPollingOrchestrator (polls only while CONNECTED), MedtronicReadGateway link gate.
edge_cases: Deactivating the pump plugin collapses state to DISCONNECTED regardless of the real radio state.
AUTH_FAILED is a latched terminal state; nothing auto-clears it except a new connect()/pair() or plugin swap.

capabilities.name: Paired-status card (both styles)
capabilities.behavior: Rendered above the style branch when `credentialStore.isPaired()`. Primary-container Card, Row: icon = CheckCircle if connectionState==CONNECTED else Bluetooth; title "Connected" if CONNECTED else "Paired"; subtitle = paired MAC address (raw, unmasked); trailing OutlinedButton "Unpair" with 16.dp LinkOff icon. `isPaired`/`pairedAddress` are plain (non-reactive) getters on the ViewModel reading EncryptedSharedPreferences on each composition — they do not themselves trigger recomposition, so the card appears/disappears only when some other observed state changes. 16.dp spacer separates it from the flow content below.
edge_cases: Non-reactive isPaired can leave a stale card until the next recomposition.
MAC address is displayed in cleartext in the UI.

capabilities.name: Central-scan screen state machine
capabilities.behavior: `CentralScanContent` picks exactly one child by ordered `when`: (1) connectionState CONNECTING or AUTHENTICATING → `ConnectingCard`; (2) connectionState AUTH_FAILED **and** selectedPump != null → `AuthFailedCard` + 16.dp spacer + `PairingCodeInput` (code retained, user can edit and retry); (3) selectedPump != null → `PairingCodeInput`; (4) else → `ScanSection`. CONNECTED is never rendered here — the outer LaunchedEffect pops the screen first. RECONNECTING, SCANNING and DISCONNECTED all fall through to ScanSection, i.e. a Tandem reconnect in progress shows the scan UI with no indication of the reconnect. Selecting a pump calls `selectPump()` which sets selectedPump and stops the scan.
edge_cases: AUTH_FAILED with selectedPump==null (e.g. a background reconnect failure) shows the plain scan UI, no error.
RECONNECTING is invisible on the pairing screen.

capabilities.name: Scan session lifecycle (ViewModel)
capabilities.behavior: `startScan()` cancels any prior scanJob, clears `discoveredPumps`, sets `isScanning=true`, then launches collection of `pumpScanner.scan()` in viewModelScope; the `finally` block sets `isScanning=false` when the flow ends or is cancelled. Each emission upserts into the list keyed by `address`: index found → replace in place; not found → append (preserves discovery order). `stopScan()` cancels the job and clears the flag. `selectPump()` stops the scan. `onCleared()` stops the scan and cancels the advertise job. There is no scan timeout at any layer — scanning runs until the user taps Stop Scan, selects a pump, or leaves the screen.
edge_cases: No scan timeout — indefinite radio use if the user leaves the screen open (job is cancelled only via onCleared/stop).
If the underlying scan flow closes with an exception (BLE scan failure), isScanning flips false with no error surfaced to the user.

capabilities.name: Tandem BLE scan implementation
capabilities.behavior: `BleScanner.scan()` is a `callbackFlow`. If `BluetoothManager.adapter?.bluetoothLeScanner` is null it closes the flow immediately (no error surface). ScanFilter = single filter on service UUID `0000fdfb-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb` (TandemProtocol.PUMP_SERVICE_UUID), ScanSettings mode `SCAN_MODE_LOW_LATENCY`, no report-delay, no timeout. A local `seen: MutableSet<String>` of addresses means each device is emitted exactly once — RSSI is never refreshed after first sight. Emitted `DiscoveredPump(name = device.name ?: "Tandem Pump", address, rssi)`. `onScanFailed(errorCode)` closes the flow with `IllegalStateException("BLE scan failed: $errorCode")`. `awaitClose` calls `scanner.stopScan(callback)`. PumpScannerAdapter maps DiscoveredDevice→DiscoveredPump with `rssi ?: 0`.
edge_cases: RSSI in the list is a one-shot snapshot, never live.
Scan-failure exception is swallowed by the ViewModel's try/finally; UI just stops showing "Scanning…".
Only devices advertising service 0xFDFB appear; a pump not in pairing mode never advertises.

capabilities.name: Scan section UI (device list, empty state, scan button)
capabilities.behavior: Static blurb: "Scan for nearby Tandem pumps. Make sure Bluetooth is enabled and your pump is in pairing mode." Full-width Button (testTag `scan_button`) with BluetoothSearching icon (20.dp); label toggles "Scan for Pumps" / "Stop Scan". While scanning: a centered 16.dp CircularProgressIndicator (strokeWidth 2.dp) + "Scanning...". When `pumps.isEmpty() && !isScanning`: "No pumps found. Tap Scan to search." Device list is a LazyColumn, 8.dp item spacing; each `PumpCard` is a clickable Card with a primary-tinted Bluetooth icon, name (titleSmall), MAC address (bodySmall, onSurfaceVariant) and right-aligned "<rssi> dBm". Tapping a card selects that pump. No sorting, no RSSI-based ordering, no signal-strength bars, no filtering beyond the service-UUID scan filter.
edge_cases: List order = discovery order, not signal strength.
Devices are never aged out of the list once seen.

capabilities.name: BLE scan runtime-permission sequence
capabilities.behavior: `requiredBlePermissions()` returns, on API ≥ 31 (Build.VERSION_CODES.S): `[BLUETOOTH_SCAN, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT]`; below 31: `[ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION]`. Flow: tapping Scan calls `hasPermissions()` (ContextCompat.checkSelfPermission on every element). If all granted → clear the denial flag and `onStartScan()`. Otherwise `rememberLauncherForActivityResult(RequestMultiplePermissions).launch(requiredBlePermissions())`. In the result callback, `results.values.all { it }` → clear flag and immediately start the scan; any denial → set `permissionDenied = true`. There is **no** pre-request rationale screen, no `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale` check anywhere in the codebase, and no deep link to app settings — the user is told to enable them manually. Permission state is remembered per-composition only (`var permissionDenied by remember`).
edge_cases: minSdk is 30, so the ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION branch only ever applies on Android 11.
Permanent denial ("Don't ask again") produces the same card with no settings shortcut.
Denial state is lost on recomposition scope teardown / navigation.

capabilities.name: Scan permission-denied card
capabilities.behavior: Rendered above the Scan button when `permissionDenied` is true: errorContainer Card, title "Bluetooth permissions required" (titleSmall, onErrorContainer), body "GlycemicGPT needs Bluetooth permissions to scan for and connect to your Tandem pump. Please grant the permissions when prompted, or enable them in your device settings." followed by an 8.dp spacer. The Scan button remains enabled and re-launches the system permission dialog on each tap.
edge_cases: Card never auto-clears until a successful grant or a fresh check.

capabilities.name: Pairing-code entry UI and validation
capabilities.behavior: `PairingCodeInput` Card: title "Enter Pairing Code" (titleMedium), model-specific instruction (bodySmall/onSurfaceVariant), then "<name> (<address>)", then an OutlinedTextField labelled "Pairing Code" (testTag `pairing_code_field`), `KeyboardType.Text`, `singleLine = true` — no numeric keypad, no masking, no per-digit boxes. Footer Row: OutlinedButton "Cancel" (weight 1f) → `clearSelection()` (clears selectedPump and code) and Button "Pair" (weight 1f, testTag `pair_button`) enabled only when `pairingCode.length >= 6`. `updatePairingCode` truncates to `code.take(16)` (comment: "up to 16 chars for legacy, 6 digits for modern"); no character-class filtering, no trimming, no case normalization. `pair()` additionally no-ops if the code is empty. No client-side verification of the code.
edge_cases: Codes of length 7–10 are accepted and routed to JPAKE; 11–16 route to legacy V1 auth (driver-side branch is `code.length <= 10`).
Whitespace/paste of a longer string is silently truncated at 16 chars.

capabilities.name: Per-model pairing instructions (Tandem)
capabilities.behavior: `TandemPumpModel.fromAdvertisedName(name)` normalizes (trim + collapse whitespace runs) and matches case-insensitively: startsWith "tslim X2" or "t:slim X2" → TSLIM_X2 (hasScreen=true); startsWith "Tandem Mobi" → MOBI (hasScreen=false); else UNKNOWN (hasScreen=null). Instruction text: hasScreen==true → "Check your pump screen for the pairing code. You must confirm pairing on the pump."; ==false → "Put your Mobi on the charging pad and double-press the pump button to enter pairing mode. Then enter the 6-digit PIN printed behind the cartridge well on your pump body."; ==null → "Enter the pairing code from your pump. Check your pump screen or documentation for the code." Memoized with `remember(pump.name)`.
edge_cases: Model detection is by BLE advertised name only; a null/renamed device falls back to the "Tandem Pump" default name and UNKNOWN instructions.
Instruction text is hard-coded Tandem regardless of which central-scan plugin is active.

capabilities.name: CONNECTING / AUTHENTICATING display
capabilities.behavior: `ConnectingCard(state)`: full-width Card, 32.dp padding, centered Column with an indeterminate CircularProgressIndicator, 16.dp spacer, and bodyLarge text — CONNECTING → "Connecting to pump...", AUTHENTICATING → "Authenticating...", any other state → "Working...". Used identically by both pairing styles. There is no cancel affordance while connecting/authenticating, no elapsed-time or timeout countdown, and no progress detail (e.g. JPAKE round). If the driver's own auth timeout (30 s) fires the state moves to AUTH_FAILED (or back to reconnect), which re-renders the screen.
edge_cases: No user-facing cancel during CONNECTING/AUTHENTICATING; the only escape is system back.
A hung driver that never leaves CONNECTING leaves the spinner up indefinitely (no UI-level timeout).

capabilities.name: AUTH_FAILED display and retry (central-scan)
capabilities.behavior: `AuthFailedCard`: errorContainer Card, title "Pairing failed", body "The pump rejected the pairing attempt. Please verify the code and try again." It is rendered above a live `PairingCodeInput` pre-filled with the previously entered code, so "Pair" re-runs `connectionManager.connect(address, code)` with the same or an edited code. The card's own `onRetry` parameter is bound to `onPair` but the card itself renders no button. Cancel clears both the selection and the code, returning to the scan list. This branch requires `selectedPump != null`; an AUTH_FAILED that arrives with no selection (background reconnect failure) shows nothing.
edge_cases: The error copy is generic — it does not distinguish wrong code from bond loss, encryption failure, or zero-response detection, all of which set AUTH_FAILED in the Tandem driver.

capabilities.name: Advertise-and-wait: idle / "Before you start" state
capabilities.behavior: `AdvertiseIdleContent` always shows a Card (testTag `single_peer_instruction`) titled "Before you start": "A pump pairs with only one phone at a time. If this pump is currently paired with the manufacturer's official app, remove it there first or it will not connect here." Then, if a fault is present, a `FaultCard`; then, if permissions were denied, the advertise-specific denial card; then a full-width Button (testTag `start_pairing_button`) with a 20.dp Bluetooth icon whose label is "Try Again" when a fault is set, otherwise "Start Pairing". Tapping it runs the advertise permission check and, if satisfied, `viewModel.startAdvertising()`.
edge_cases: Faults persist in the idle state until the next `beginAdvertising()` clears `_fault`, so "Try Again" is the only way to clear the message.

capabilities.name: Advertise runtime-permission sequence (deliberate pre-31 decision)
capabilities.behavior: `requiredAdvertisePermissions()` returns on API ≥ 31: `[BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE, BLUETOOTH_CONNECT]`; below 31 it returns an **empty array**. Documented reason in-code: pre-Android-12 advertising uses the auto-granted legacy BLUETOOTH/BLUETOOTH_ADMIN install-time permissions, and ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is a *scanning* requirement, not an advertising one — "requesting it here would pop a needless dialog that, if denied, blocks pairing even though advertising would work." With an empty array `all{}` is vacuously true, so pre-31 devices start advertising immediately with no dialog. BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE is declared only in the Medtronic plugin module manifest (`plugins/shipped/medtronic/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`, `tools:targetApi="s"`) and merged into the app manifest; the host app requests it at runtime.
edge_cases: Empty permission array on API 30 also means `launcher.launch(emptyArray())` would never be reached; the granted-branch always wins.
Advertise permissions live in a plugin manifest, so an app build without the Medtronic module lacks BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE entirely.

capabilities.name: Advertise permission-denied card
capabilities.behavior: Distinct copy from the scan variant: errorContainer Card, title "Bluetooth permissions required", body "GlycemicGPT needs Bluetooth permissions to make your phone discoverable to the pump. Please grant the permissions when prompted, or enable them in your device settings.", 8.dp spacer, then the Start Pairing/Try Again button. Set when `results.values.all { it }` is false in the RequestMultiplePermissions callback; cleared when a subsequent check or grant succeeds.
edge_cases: No settings deep link, same as the scan variant.

capabilities.name: Advertise-and-wait: waiting state card
capabilities.behavior: `AdvertisingCard` (testTag `advertising_status`): centered Row with a 16.dp/2.dp-stroke CircularProgressIndicator and titleSmall "Waiting for your pump"; body text — when advertisedName != null: "Your phone is now discoverable as \"<name>\". On your pump, open the pairing menu (Add/Pair new device) and select \"<name>\" to connect."; else the generic "Your phone is now discoverable. On your pump, open the pairing menu and select this phone to connect." If `fault == BOUND_ELSEWHERE`, an error-coloured line (testTag `pairing_fault`) with that fault's message is appended after a 12.dp spacer while the spinner keeps running. Footer: full-width OutlinedButton "Cancel" (testTag `cancel_advertising_button`) → `stopAdvertising()`.
edge_cases: No countdown shown even though the driver arms a 60 s BOUND_ELSEWHERE timer.
Waiting persists indefinitely until Cancel or a pump connects.

capabilities.name: Advertise-and-wait phase routing rule (documented decision)
capabilities.behavior: `terminalFault = fault != null && fault != PairingFault.BOUND_ELSEWHERE`. Routing `when`: (1) CONNECTING or AUTHENTICATING → ConnectingCard; (2) connectionState == SCANNING **or** (`isAdvertising && !terminalFault && connectionState == DISCONNECTED`) → AdvertisingCard; (3) else → AdvertiseIdleContent. Stated rationale in-code: the phase is driven off the manager's connection state, not the advertise job's liveness, because "the scan flow stays open across terminal faults and a completed handshake, so it can't be the source of truth"; only TERMINAL faults route to idle so they surface a message + Try Again "instead of an endless 'Waiting' spinner", while BOUND_ELSEWHERE means "still advertising, nothing has connected yet" and stays in the waiting state where Cancel is shown.
edge_cases: AUTH_FAILED (a terminal fault) routes to the idle content, where the FaultCard + Try Again appear.
RECONNECTING for an advertise-and-wait pump also lands in idle content.

capabilities.name: PairingFault taxonomy and user-facing messages
capabilities.behavior: `enum PairingFault { PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED, ADVERTISE_FAILED, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, AUTH_FAILED, BOUND_ELSEWHERE }`, only ever non-null for advertise-and-wait plugins (central-scan plugins hard-code null). `faultMessage()`: PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED → "This phone can't act as a Bluetooth accessory, so it can't pair with this pump. A different phone may be required."; ADVERTISE_FAILED → "Couldn't start Bluetooth advertising. Close other Bluetooth apps and try again."; HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT → "The pump connected but the secure handshake timed out. Try again."; AUTH_FAILED → "The pump rejected the secure handshake. Try again."; BOUND_ELSEWHERE → "No pump has connected yet. If this pump is still paired with the manufacturer's official app, remove it there first." `FaultCard` wraps the message with header "Pairing did not complete" in an errorContainer Card (testTag `pairing_fault`). Mapped 1:1 from `MedtronicConnectionFault` (BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED → BOUND_ELSEWHERE).
edge_cases: Two different composables carry testTag `pairing_fault` (inline text in the waiting card, and the FaultCard).

capabilities.name: Advertise job lifecycle and isAdvertising flag ownership
capabilities.behavior: `startAdvertising()` cancels the previous advertiseJob, sets `_isAdvertising = true`, then launches `pumpScanner.scan().collect { }` — collection alone keeps advertising alive; emissions signal that a pump connected, after which the connection manager owns the lifecycle. The `finally` block resets the flag **only** when `coroutineContext[Job]?.isCancelled != true`, so a stale cancelled job can never clobber newer state — cancellation callers (`stopAdvertising()`, a superseding `startAdvertising()`) own the flag themselves. A device that cannot advertise closes the flow immediately, so `isAdvertising` flips back to false and `pairingFault` reports PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED. `stopAdvertising()` cancels the job and sets the flag false; it deliberately does not touch the foreground service because the service is only started once a session forms.
edge_cases: Re-pair for an already-paired Medtronic pump always goes through scan() → FIRST_PAIR advertising; the plugin's `forceFirstPair` config key is unreachable from the pairing UI.
onCleared() cancels the advertise job, so navigating away silently stops advertising.

capabilities.name: Foreground-service coupling to session formation (documented decision)
capabilities.behavior: `PairingViewModel.init` collects `connectionState` and calls `PumpConnectionService.start(appContext)` whenever the state is in `SESSION_LIVE_OR_FORMING = {CONNECTING, AUTHENTICATING, CONNECTED}`. Documented reason: starting the service on the "Start Pairing" tap and stopping it when advertising can't even begin (a phone that can't act as a BLE peripheral, where `scan()` closes immediately) crashes with `ForegroundServiceDidNotStartInTime` — the service is torn down before it can promote itself. So the service starts only once a pump is actually connecting/connected, so polling is ready and survives navigation away, and is stopped on unpair. Explicitly noted as safe and idempotent for Tandem, whose `pair()` already calls `PumpConnectionService.start()` at its own connection point.
edge_cases: Advertising that ends without a session never starts or stops the service (asserted by tests).

The service is also started from GlycemicGptApp.onCreate and BootCompletedReceiver whenever `pumpCredentialStore.isPaired()`, and from SettingsViewModel.loadState() on every Settings open while paired.

capabilities.name: Unpair from the pairing screen
capabilities.behavior: `PairingViewModel.unpair()` → `connectionManager.unpair()` (adapter → `activePumpPlugin.asPumpStatus().unpair()` → driver-level unpair: clear credentials + remove OS bond + disconnect), then `PumpConnectionService.stop(appContext)`, then clears `selectedPump` and `pairingCode`. This is the *full* unpair path. There is no confirmation dialog on the pairing screen — the Unpair button acts immediately.
edge_cases: If no pump plugin is active, `unpair()` silently no-ops (null-safe chain) while the service is still stopped.
No confirmation — a mis-tap immediately drops the pairing and the BLE bond.

capabilities.name: Unpair from Settings (divergent, weaker path)
capabilities.behavior: Settings pump card → "Unpair" opens an AlertDialog: title "Unpair Pump", text "Are you sure you want to unpair this pump? You will need to re-pair to resume data collection.", confirm "Unpair" (error-coloured TextButton), dismiss "Cancel". Confirming calls `SettingsViewModel.unpair()`, which **only** does `pumpCredentialStore.clearPairing()` and updates the UI state (`isPumpPaired=false`, `pairedPumpAddress=null`). It does not call `connectionManager.unpair()`, does not remove the BLE bond, does not disconnect, and does not stop `PumpConnectionService` — unlike the pairing-screen path. `SettingsViewModel.logout()` does stop the service.
edge_cases: Settings unpair leaves a live BLE session, a running foreground service, and a stale OS bond; the driver may keep reconnecting until it fails credential lookup.
The two unpair entry points have materially different effects — a port must decide which is canonical.

capabilities.name: Settings pump card (pairing status + entry points)
capabilities.behavior: Rendered whenever `state.activePumpPluginId != null` (registry resolves the active PUMP_STATUS/INSULIN_SOURCE plugin generically — no vendor hard-coding). Row: Bluetooth icon if paired else BluetoothDisabled (24.dp, primary tint); title = active plugin name or "Insulin Pump"; subtitle = "Paired: <address>" or "Not paired". Below, plugin-contributed InfoText notes only (testTag `pump_settings_notes`) — Medtronic contributes "A MiniMed pump pairs with only one phone at a time. Remove the pump from the official Medtronic app before pairing it here."; Tandem contributes an empty descriptor. Actions: paired → Row of "Re-pair" (testTag `repair_button`) and error-coloured "Unpair" (testTag `unpair_button`); unpaired → full-width "Pair Pump" (testTag `pair_pump_button`). Metadata and descriptor reads are each wrapped in `catch (Throwable)` so a misbehaving plugin degrades rather than crashes settings.
edge_cases: Descriptor is reduced to InfoText items only (`infoNotesOnly()`); interactive plugin settings never render on the pump card.
No pump plugin active → no pump card at all, so there is no way to reach the pairing screen.

capabilities.name: Tandem connect + authentication state machine
capabilities.behavior: `connect(address, code?)` (resetCounters=true) cancels pending reconnects, closes the passive autoConnect GATT, sets CONNECTING, clears queues/assemblers/pending requests, stores `pendingPairingCode`, and calls `device.connectGatt(context, false, cb, TRANSPORT_LE)`. On GATT connect: `refresh()` the service cache (reflection), `requestConnectionPriority(HIGH)`, `requestMtu(185)`. On MTU success → `discoverServices()`; failure → close + DISCONNECTED. On services discovered: enable CCCD on AUTHORIZATION (7B83FFF9…), set AUTHENTICATING, start auth, then enqueue the remaining 5 notification CCCDs. Auth branch: `code.length <= 10` → JPAKE (CONFIRMATION if reconnect and a saved derived secret exists, else BOOTSTRAP 5 round trips); longer → legacy V1 challenge. Success → `onAuthSuccess()`: save pairing + JPAKE secret/nonce, send init opcodes, and after `POST_AUTH_SETTLE_MS = 500` set CONNECTED (only if still AUTHENTICATING).
edge_cases: Missing code (no pending code and none stored) → immediate AUTH_FAILED.
JPAKE round-3 or round-4 failure clears saved JPAKE credentials so the next attempt falls back to BOOTSTRAP (requires pump pairing mode).
Auth handshake timeout `AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000`: if a prior successful session existed, it disconnects and lets the reconnect path run; otherwise sets AUTH_FAILED.

capabilities.name: Tandem reconnect policy (two-phase, indefinite)
capabilities.behavior: `scheduleReconnect()` sets RECONNECTING and picks a delay under `autoConnectLock`. FAST phase: `reconnectAttempt = min(attempt+1, 10)`; delay = `min(1000 * 2^min(attempt,5), 32_000)` ms → 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, 32 s… After `MAX_FAST_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 10` (~5 min) it switches to SLOW: opens a passive `connectGatt(autoConnect=true)` handled by the kernel BLE stack and retries every `SLOW_RECONNECT_INTERVAL_MS = 120_000` ms **indefinitely** — stated rationale: "The pump is a medical device — if the user hasn't explicitly unpaired, we should always try to reconnect." The autoConnect callback, on a successful kernel-level reconnect, closes itself and calls `connectInternal(..., resetCounters=false)`. `onAuthSuccess()` resets attempt counters and returns to FAST. `autoReconnectIfPaired()` forces FAST and reconnects with `pairingCode = null` (JPAKE confirmation mode).
edge_cases: `consecutiveReconnectFailures` is capped at `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_RECONNECT_FAILURES = 100` and used for logging only — it never stops the loop.
autoConnect GATT is closed on every explicit connect and reopened on each slow-phase schedule.

capabilities.name: Tandem bond-loss / AUTH_FAILED heuristics (safety-relevant)
capabilities.behavior: On GATT disconnect, `wasConnected` = state was CONNECTED or AUTHENTICATING. Status `0x13` (CONN_TERMINATE_PEER_USER) before CONNECTED: if `hadSuccessfulSession` it is treated as idle-timeout and reconnection continues; else `rapidDisconnectCount++` and at `MAX_RAPID_DISCONNECTS = 3` → stop auto-reconnect, AUTH_FAILED. Status `0x05` (INSUFFICIENT_AUTHENTICATION) before CONNECTED → remove bond, AUTH_FAILED immediately. Status `0x08` (INSUFFICIENT_ENCRYPTION): if never fully connected and no prior session → remove bond + AUTH_FAILED; otherwise the bond is **never** removed (explicit: removing it would force a manual re-pair with the pump in pairing mode) and `encryptionFailureCount` accumulates to `MAX_ENCRYPTION_FAILURES = 20` before reporting AUTH_FAILED with the bond preserved. Reaching CONNECTED with zero notifications `MAX_ZERO_RESPONSE_CONNECTIONS = 3` times → remove bond + AUTH_FAILED.
edge_cases: `hadSuccessfulSession` is reset only by user-initiated disconnect()/unpair(), deliberately surviving reconnect cycles.
All of these paths surface to the user only as the generic "Pairing failed" copy.

capabilities.name: Tandem unpair and bond removal
capabilities.behavior: `BleConnectionManager.unpair()`: read the stored address, `disconnect()` (autoReconnect=false, hadSuccessfulSession=false, cancel reconnect/auth/settle jobs, clear queues + pending requests, close GATT, state DISCONNECTED), `credentialStore.clearPairing()` (clears the entire encrypted prefs file including JPAKE secret/nonce), then `removeBond(address)` via reflection on the hidden `BluetoothDevice.removeBond()` (only when bondState == BOND_BONDED; failures logged at WARN), then cancel the autoConnect GATT. `refreshGattCache()` uses the same reflection trick on `BluetoothGatt.refresh()` at every connect to avoid stale cached characteristics silently dropping notifications.
edge_cases: Both reflection calls are hidden-API dependent and fail soft (logged, ignored).

capabilities.name: Medtronic advertise-and-wait connection state machine
capabilities.behavior: All lifecycle mutation is posted onto a single `SerialWorker` (HandlerThread "medtronic-sake"). `startSession(forceFirstPair)`: if `!peripheral.isSupported()` set fault PERIPHERAL_UNSUPPORTED + DISCONNECTED; else `advertisingModeFor(isPaired, forceFirstPair)` (RECONNECT only when paired and not forced) and `beginAdvertising(mode, CONNECTING)`. `scan()` (the pairing-UI path) advertises FIRST_PAIR with state SCANNING, sets autoReconnect=false, and on `awaitClose` tears down only if still SCANNING. `onCentralConnected` cancels the pairing-wait timer, clears fault, stops advertising (single-peer), and moves SCANNING/CONNECTING/RECONNECTING → CONNECTING, emitting a DiscoveredDevice. `onSakeSubscribed` → AUTHENTICATING + arm auth timeout + drive SAKE. Handshake complete → save pairing (address, localName as the "code" slot) + CONNECTED. Disconnect while autoReconnect && paired → RECONNECTING + re-advertise RECONNECT; else teardown to DISCONNECTED.
edge_cases: AUTH_FAILED is latched: the ensuing disconnect must not reset it or start a reconnect loop against a pump that just rejected us.
SAKE has no pairing code; the credential store's code slot records the advertised identity instead.

capabilities.name: Medtronic timers, advertising parameters and UUIDs
capabilities.behavior: `DEFAULT_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (six 20-byte SAKE round trips); on expiry while AUTHENTICATING → fault HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT, state AUTH_FAILED, autoReconnect=false, stop advertising. `DEFAULT_PAIRING_WAIT_MS = 60_000`, armed only for FIRST_PAIR advertising; if still CONNECTING or SCANNING when it fires → fault BOUND_ELSEWHERE_SUSPECTED (state unchanged). RECONNECT mode waits indefinitely because the pump scans infrequently. Advertising: FIRST_PAIR = service `0xFE82` at `ADVERTISE_MODE_BALANCED`; RECONNECT = `0xFE81` at `ADVERTISE_MODE_LOW_LATENCY`; both connectable, timeout 0 (until stopped), `ADVERTISE_TX_POWER_MEDIUM`, device name excluded (31-byte budget), TX power included, name carried in manufacturer data under company id `0x01F9`. `DEFAULT_LOCAL_NAME = "Mobile 000001"` (must match `Mobile .{0,7}`). GATT server (Device Info + SAKE) is opened and its services registered before advertising starts.
edge_cases: Advertised name is a hard-coded constant — two phones running the app advertise the same name (TODO: per-install identity).
SAKE characteristic UUID uses the Medtronic vendor base (…-0000-1000-0000-009132591325) with short code 0xFE82; an earlier SIG-based form left the pump unable to find the characteristic (issue #844).
`isSupported()` requires adapter enabled + `isMultipleAdvertisementSupported` + a non-null advertiser.

capabilities.name: Medtronic unpair / disconnect / shutdown semantics
capabilities.behavior: `disconnect()`: autoReconnect=false + teardown(DISCONNECTED, fault=null) — stops advertising, closes the GATT server, drops the SAKE session, keeps the pairing. `unpair()`: resolve address from stored pairing or the connected peer, autoReconnect=false, teardown, `credentialStore.clearPairing()`, then best-effort `peripheral.removeBond(address)` (reflection on the hidden `removeBond()`). `close()` (only from `Plugin.shutdown()`) runs teardown synchronously on the caller thread — because a posted teardown could be dropped as the worker stops — then stops the worker and cancels the scope; the manager is unusable afterwards. `onActivated()` calls `reconnectIfPaired()`; `onDeactivated()` calls `disconnect()` (deliberately not `close()`, so reactivating reconnects without re-pairing).
edge_cases: `reconnectIfPaired()` is a no-op when nothing is paired.
Tandem's equivalent hooks are `onActivated → autoReconnectIfPaired()` and `onDeactivated → disconnect()`.

capabilities.name: Pairing credential persistence
capabilities.behavior: `PumpCredentialStore` implements `PumpCredentialProvider` over `EncryptedSharedPreferences` file "pump_credentials", master key `MasterKeys.AES256_GCM_SPEC`, key scheme `AES256_SIV`, value scheme `AES256_GCM`. Keys: `paired_pump_address`, `pairing_code`, `paired_at` (epoch millis, written on savePairing, never read), `jpake_derived_secret`, `jpake_server_nonce` (hex strings). `isPaired()` = address != null. `savePairing(address, code)` writes address + code + timestamp. `clearJpakeCredentials()` removes only the two JPAKE keys (used when confirmation mode is rejected, so the next attempt bootstraps). `clearPairing()` calls `prefs.edit().clear()` — wiping everything including JPAKE material.
edge_cases: A single store is shared by all pump plugins — pairing a second driver overwrites the first driver's address/code.
Medtronic stores the advertised local name in the `pairing_code` slot.

capabilities.name: PumpConnectionService: foreground service + wake-lock policy
capabilities.behavior: Channel `pump_connection` ("Pump Connection", IMPORTANCE_LOW, no badge), NOTIFICATION_ID 1, ongoing + silent, small icon `stat_sys_data_bluetooth`, `START_STICKY`. `onStartCommand` calls `startForeground` from the cached floor status, then (once per lifecycle) starts polling + backend sync, calls `connectionManager.autoReconnectIfPaired()`, and registers receivers. Wake-lock watcher on connectionState: CONNECTED → PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK tagged "GlycemicGPT:PumpBleConnection" with `WAKE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 20 min` plus a renewal loop every `WAKE_LOCK_RENEW_MS = 15 min`; RECONNECTING/CONNECTING/AUTHENTICATING → shorter `RECONNECT_WAKE_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 2 min` (covers 32 s max backoff + GATT + JPAKE); anything else → release. Battery receiver: `pct < 15` sets `pollingOrchestrator.phoneBatteryLow`; `pct < 5` releases the wake lock; recovery re-acquires the state-appropriate lock.
edge_cases: Wake lock is `setReferenceCounted(false)`; re-acquire simply refreshes the timeout.
Critical-battery release can silently stop the 15 s keep-alive polls (pump drops idle BLE links at ~30 s).

capabilities.name: Bluetooth adapter state watcher → auto-reconnect
capabilities.behavior: PumpConnectionService registers an exported receiver for `BluetoothAdapter.ACTION_STATE_CHANGED`. On `STATE_ON` it calls `connectionManager.autoReconnectIfPaired()` (Tandem: reset to FAST phase and reconnect with a null pairing code, i.e. JPAKE confirmation mode; Medtronic: `reconnectIfPaired()` → RECONNECT-mode advertising). On `STATE_OFF`/`STATE_TURNING_OFF` it only logs — GATT callbacks handle the disconnection. The battery receiver is registered `RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED`; the Bluetooth receiver `RECEIVER_EXPORTED`. Both are unregistered in `onDestroy` with IllegalArgumentException swallowed.
edge_cases: Turning Bluetooth off produces no user-facing pairing/connection message beyond the Home status icon flipping to DISCONNECTED.

capabilities.name: Foreground-notification honesty text (alert-floor coupling)
capabilities.behavior: Content title is always `pump_service_notification_title` = "Connected to pump". Content text is derived from `AlertFloorStatus`: ServerActive → "Reading pump data in background"; FloorWatching → "Server alerts paused — this phone is watching for lows and highs" when a backend is configured, else "This phone is watching for lows and highs" (BLE-only mode must not imply a server exists); FloorNotWatching → "Alerts degraded — this phone is NOT watching for lows or highs". The last status is cached in `lastFloorStatus` (seeded pessimistically in `onCreate`) so redundant service starts — e.g. every Settings open while paired — cannot overwrite an honest "NOT watching" with the default copy. The watcher catches non-cancellation exceptions and freezes the text rather than killing the pump service.
edge_cases: Title says "Connected to pump" even while DISCONNECTED/RECONNECTING.
Status text is always on the silent low-importance channel — never an alarm.

capabilities.name: Home-screen connection status surface
capabilities.behavior: `ConnectionSyncRow` (testTag `connection_status`) renders a 16.dp icon + optional label per state: CONNECTED → BluetoothConnected, primary tint, a11y "Pump connected", no label; CONNECTING/AUTHENTICATING → BluetoothSearching, tertiary, "Connecting..."; RECONNECTING → Bluetooth, tertiary, "Reconnecting..."; SCANNING → BluetoothSearching, tertiary, "Scanning..."; AUTH_FAILED → BluetoothDisabled, error, "Pairing failed"; DISCONNECTED → BluetoothDisabled, error, no label. Below the cards, DISCONNECTED additionally shows "Pair your pump in Settings to start"; CONNECTED with no CGM reading shows "Loading pump data..." in tertiary. `HomeViewModel.connectionState` is `pumpDriver.observeConnectionState().stateIn(WhileSubscribed(5000), DISCONNECTED)`.
edge_cases: AUTH_FAILED on Home is not tappable — there is no shortcut to re-pair from the status row.
CONNECTED/DISCONNECTED carry no text label, only icon + contentDescription.

capabilities.name: Plugin activation gate on the pairing surface
capabilities.behavior: `PluginRegistry.updateStateFlows()` sets `activePumpPlugin` to the first active plugin declaring PUMP_STATUS or INSULIN_SOURCE, cast to DevicePlugin. There is **no default activation**: `initialize()` creates plugins from compile-time factories (skipping any with a mismatched `PLUGIN_API_VERSION` or disabled by the feature gate) then `restoreActivePlugins()` only restores IDs previously persisted per capability. Activation is mutually exclusive for SINGLE_INSTANCE capabilities: the new plugin is activated first (slot never empty), preferences are written, then the conflicting plugin is deactivated (its `onDeactivated()` disconnects). Shipped plugin ids: `com.glycemicgpt.tandem`, `com.glycemicgpt.medtronic`. Settings "Available Plugins" is the only place to switch drivers.
edge_cases: Fresh install with no plugin activated: no pump card in Settings, hence no route to the pairing screen at all.
Switching drivers while paired leaves the other driver's credentials in the shared store.

capabilities.name: Declared BLE-related manifest permissions and platform floor
capabilities.behavior: App manifest declares `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT`; `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` with `usesPermissionFlags="neverForLocation"` (`tools:targetApi="s"`); `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` and `ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION` both with `android:maxSdkVersion="30"`; `FOREGROUND_SERVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_CONNECTED_DEVICE`, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC`, `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`, `WAKE_LOCK`, `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS`, `RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED`. `uses-feature android.hardware.bluetooth_le` is `required="true"`. `BLUETOOTH_ADVERTISE` comes only from the Medtronic plugin module manifest via merge. Build config: compileSdk 35, minSdk 30, targetSdk 35. ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION is declared but never requested at runtime.
edge_cases: minSdk 30 means the location-permission branch only applies on Android 11.

capabilities.name: Adjacent permission surfaces reached from the pairing journey
capabilities.behavior: POST_NOTIFICATIONS: Settings → Notifications shows `NotificationStatusCard` with a live `checkSelfPermission` (pre-33 always granted), re-checked on `ON_RESUME`. "Enable" launches `Settings.ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS` with `EXTRA_APP_PACKAGE` — it does **not** use the runtime permission launcher — falling back to a long Toast on ActivityNotFoundException/SecurityException. Copy when denied: "Disabled -- alerts will not appear on your phone". Battery optimization: when `isPumpPaired && isBatteryOptimized`, Settings shows a warning card "Battery Optimization Active" / "Android may stop the pump connection when the screen is off. Disable battery optimization for reliable overnight monitoring." whose action fires `Settings.ACTION_REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` with `package:` URI; status is re-read via `PowerManager.isIgnoringBatteryOptimizations`.
edge_cases: Onboarding (WELCOME/FEATURES/DISCLAIMER/SERVER/LOGIN, 5 pages) contains no BLE permission or pairing step — pairing is entirely a post-onboarding Settings action.

capabilities.name: Documented user-facing pairing behavior (shipped docs)
capabilities.behavior: `docs/troubleshooting/cant-pair-pump.md`: prerequisites (Bluetooth on, Location enabled on Android 11, pump in pairing mode — Tandem t:slim X2 Options → Bluetooth Settings → Pair Device, code times out "after a couple of minutes", pump within a couple of metres); "app must be scanning before the pump starts advertising"; Tandem allows one Bluetooth connection at a time; requires Android 11+ (API 30+); battery-optimization guidance including Samsung "Sleeping apps"; Mobi is documented as unverified against physical hardware. `docs/daily-use/connecting-medtronic-pump.md`: explicitly BETA and read-only, single-peer removal from MiniMed Mobile required first, advertise-and-wait named "Mobile 000001", 5-step flow, and the four fault messages with remedies; "Once paired, the pump is remembered — GlycemicGPT reconnects on its own."
edge_cases: The troubleshooting doc claims the app "shows two fields during pairing -- one for the pump's code, one to confirm"; the shipped UI has a single code field. Doc/code drift.

safety_critical: BLE bond removal decisions (Tandem BleConnectionManager.onConnectionStateChange): status 0x05 before CONNECTED, status 0x08 with no prior successful session, and 3 consecutive zero-response connections all call removeBond() + latch AUTH_FAILED. A wrong removal forces a manual re-pair with the pump physically in pairing mode, so the app stops reading glucose/insulin until the user notices. The explicit counter-rule — never remove the bond when hadSuccessfulSession is true, because transient sleep/wake encryption renegotiation resolves itself — is load-bearing and must be ported exactly.

Indefinite reconnection is a deliberate safety decision: after MAX_FAST_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS = 10 (~5 min of 1–32 s exponential backoff) the Tandem driver switches to SLOW phase (every 120 s + passive autoConnect GATT) and retries forever unless the user unpairs. Stated reason: "The pump is a medical device." Any port that gives up after N attempts silently stops glucose monitoring.

AUTH_FAILED is a latched terminal state in both drivers with only generic user copy ("Pairing failed" / "The pump rejected the pairing attempt"). Bond loss, stale encryption keys, a pump that ignores requests, and a mistyped code are indistinguishable to the user, so a patient can be left with no data and no actionable message.

PumpConnectionService wake-lock and battery thresholds directly gate whether BLE keep-alive polling (15 s cadence; pump drops idle links at ~30 s) survives screen-off. Releasing the wake lock below 5% battery and reducing polling below 15% can silently stop data flow and therefore stop the on-phone alert floor from seeing new readings.

Foreground-notification honesty text is the only backgrounded surface that states whether anything is watching for lows/highs. lastFloorStatus caching exists specifically so redundant service starts cannot replace "Alerts degraded — this phone is NOT watching for lows or highs" with all-is-well copy. Losing that guarantee in a port would produce a false safety claim.

Settings unpair (SettingsViewModel.unpair) clears credentials only — it leaves a live BLE session, a running foreground service, and the OS bond intact, unlike the pairing-screen unpair. A user who "unpairs" from Settings may believe the pump is disconnected while the app keeps a session; conversely the driver may keep reconnecting with no stored credentials.

Single-peer constraint for both vendors: pairing here requires removing the pump from the manufacturer's official app. If a user pairs GlycemicGPT while relying on the official app for alerts, they can lose the vendor's alerting. This is surfaced in the Medtronic pairing screen, the Medtronic settings note, and both docs.

Medtronic pairing is BETA / read-only and not validated against live pumps for several paths (TODO markers on the 60 s BOUND_ELSEWHERE window, the hard-coded advertised name, and live re-confirmation of the SAKE characteristic UUID after issue #844). The driver declares no PUMP_CONTROL capability and never writes to the pump.

Pairing credentials (address, pairing code, JPAKE derived secret and server nonce) live in one shared EncryptedSharedPreferences file (AES256_SIV keys / AES256_GCM values). clearPairing() wipes the whole file. The MAC address is displayed unmasked in both the pairing screen and Settings.

Hidden-API reflection is used for BluetoothDevice.removeBond() (both drivers) and BluetoothGatt.refresh() (Tandem). Both fail soft with a WARN log; a silent failure of refresh() can cause notifications to be dropped from a stale GATT cache, which presents as a connected pump delivering no data.
map.notes:
Coverage is complete for the stated scope at uniform depth: the whole of presentation/pairing (PairingScreen.kt 775 lines, PairingViewModel.kt 188 lines, PairingViewModelTest.kt), the connection orchestration it drives (PumpConnectionAdapter, PumpScannerAdapter, PumpConnectionManager/PumpScanner/DevicePlugin contracts, PluginRegistry activation, PumpConnectionService, GlycemicGptApp/BootCompletedReceiver auto-start), both shipped driver state machines (Tandem BleConnectionManager + BleScanner; Medtronic MedtronicBleConnectionManager + AndroidMedtronicPeripheral + SakeHandshakeDriver), the credential store, and every runtime-permission path.

Deliberate scope calls: I covered the two driver state machines at the level needed to reproduce the states/timers/thresholds the UI renders, not their wire protocols (JPAKE/SAKE crypto, packetization, history parsing) — those belong to a BLE-protocol pass. PumpPollingOrchestrator is referenced only where it gates on ConnectionState (polls only while CONNECTED; INTERVAL_FAST_MS 15_000, LOW_BATTERY_MULTIPLIER 3).

Three concrete divergences a Swift port must resolve rather than copy blindly: (1) two unpair paths with different effects (pairing screen = full teardown + bond removal + service stop; Settings = credential clear only); (2) the Medtronic `forceFirstPair` config key is defined on the plugin but unreachable from the pairing UI, so every Medtronic re-pair advertises FIRST_PAIR via scan(); (3) the troubleshooting doc describes a two-field pairing-code entry that the shipped UI does not have.

There are no ADRs on pairing; the load-bearing decisions are captured as in-code comments and I have quoted their stated reasons verbatim where they exist (foreground-service start point, advertise-permission omission pre-API-31, terminal-vs-BOUND_ELSEWHERE phase routing, never-remove-bond-after-successful-session, indefinite reconnect).

There is no pairing or connection-management surface on the Wear module — the watch only renders forwarded monitoring status.

port.subsystem: Pairing UX and connection lifecycle surface (PairingScreen/PairingViewModel, app-side connection orchestration, BLE runtime-permission flow, both shipped driver connection state machines) — iOS 18+/watchOS 11+ Swift port analysis

ports_cleanly.ios_approach: SwiftUI NavigationStack with a `.pairing` path value pushed from Settings → pump card ("Pair Pump" / "Re-pair"). Android's `spokeRoutes` bottom-nav suppression maps to pushing the pairing view onto a stack inside the tab (hides the tab bar) or presenting it as a full-screen cover. The `LaunchedEffect(connectionState) { onPaired() }` auto-pop maps to `.onChange(of: connectionState) { if $0 == .connected { path.removeLast() } }` — identical semantics, including popping when the screen is not on top. Settings' `LifecycleEventEffect(ON_RESUME) { loadState() }` maps to `.onAppear` plus a `scenePhase == .active` observer. Unlike Android, iOS renders a system back chevron by default; keep it (strict parity on "no back affordance" is a regression on iOS, not a feature).

`PairingProfile(style:advertisedName:)` becomes a Swift struct returned by each compile-time-linked driver module conforming to a `DeviceDriver` protocol. `PairingStyle` stays a two-case enum (`.centralScan`, `.advertiseAndWait`). The `registry.activePumpPlugin` StateFlow becomes an `@Published var activeDriver: (any DeviceDriver)?` on an `@Observable` DriverRegistry; the pairing view switches on `activeDriver?.pairingProfile ?? .init()` so swapping drivers in Settings still changes the flow live. No default active driver → `.centralScan` default UI with a no-op scan, same silent behaviour. The hard-coded Tandem copy in the central-scan branch must move into the driver's profile (`scanBlurb`, `codeInstructions`) — a straight fix carried by the same struct.

`enum ConnectionState { disconnected, scanning, connecting, authenticating, authFailed, connected, reconnecting }` — a direct Swift enum. `PumpConnectionAdapter`'s `flatMapLatest` over the active driver becomes an `@Observable` `ConnectionCoordinator` holding `private(set) var state` fed from the active driver's `AsyncStream<ConnectionState>` (or a Combine `switchToLatest`), started eagerly on `@MainActor`. Same consumers: pairing view, home status row, BLE debug view, polling orchestrator gate, read gateway link gate. Same edge cases preserved: deactivating the driver collapses to `.disconnected`; `.authFailed` stays latched until a new `connect()`/`pair()` or driver swap.

ports_cleanly.capability: Central-scan screen state machine (ordered branch selection)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: A computed `enum CentralScanPhase` on the view model reproducing the ordered `when`: (1) `.connecting`/`.authenticating` → ConnectingCard; (2) `.authFailed` && selectedPump != nil → AuthFailedCard + code input with the code retained; (3) selectedPump != nil → code input; (4) else scan section. `.connected` is never rendered (outer auto-pop wins). Keep the documented fall-through: `.reconnecting`, `.scanning`, `.disconnected` all render the scan section. Recommend surfacing `.reconnecting` (currently invisible) as an ios_requirement rather than replicating the gap.

ports_cleanly.capability: Scan session lifecycle (start/stop/select/teardown, upsert by identity)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: `startScan()` cancels the prior `Task`, clears `discoveredPumps`, sets `isScanning = true`, and iterates the driver's `AsyncStream<DiscoveredPump>`; a `defer` block restores `isScanning = false` on completion or cancellation — exact 1:1 with the Kotlin try/finally. Upsert keyed by device identity (now `CBPeripheral.identifier`, see Tandem scan entry) preserving discovery order. `stopScan()` cancels; `selectPump()` stops the scan; `deinit`/`.onDisappear` stops scan and advertising. Swift structured concurrency gives the same cancellation semantics as `viewModelScope`.

SwiftUI `Card` + `TextField("Pairing Code")` with `.accessibilityIdentifier("pairing_code_field")`. Preserve exactly: `.take(16)` truncation in the setter, Pair enabled only at `count >= 6`, `pair()` no-ops on empty, no character-class filtering / trimming / case normalisation, no client-side verification. Cancel clears selection + code. Keep `KeyboardType.Text` equivalent (`.default`, not `.numberPad`) — the 11–16-char legacy V1 branch requires non-numeric input, so a numeric keypad would silently break legacy pairing. Add `.textInputAutocapitalization(.never)` and `.autocorrectionDisabled()`, which Android got for free from the platform.

ports_cleanly.capability: Per-model pairing instructions (Tandem t:slim X2 / Mobi / unknown)

The name source is `advertisementData[CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey] as? String ?? peripheral.name` — Core Bluetooth surfaces the advertised local name in `didDiscover`, so detection fidelity is preserved. Three instruction strings port verbatim (hasScreen true/false/nil). Memoise with a stored property on the selected-pump model instead of `remember(pump.name)`.

Error-tinted card ("Pairing failed" / "The pump rejected the pairing attempt. Please verify the code and try again.") rendered above a live code field pre-filled with the previous code, so Pair re-runs `connect(identity:code:)`. Cancel clears selection and code. ports_cleanly.capability: Advertise-and-wait idle / "Before you start" single-peer card
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Static card (`single_peer_instruction`) with the unchanged single-peer copy, then optional FaultCard, then optional permission-denied card, then a full-width button labelled "Try Again" when a fault is set else "Start Pairing". Fault persists in idle until the next start clears it. Pure SwiftUI; no platform constraint. The copy is more important on iOS, not less: with no way to remove a stale bond programmatically, removing the pump from the vendor app first is the only reliable path.

ports_cleanly.capability: Advertise-and-wait phase routing rule (terminal-fault vs BOUND_ELSEWHERE)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: Port the documented rule unchanged: `terminalFault = fault != nil && fault != .boundElsewhere`; route (1) `.connecting`/`.authenticating` → ConnectingCard, (2) `.scanning` || (isAdvertising && !terminalFault && state == .disconnected) → AdvertisingCard, (3) else idle. The stated rationale — drive phase off connection state, not advertise-job liveness — holds on iOS for the same reason (`CBPeripheralManager.isAdvertising` stays true across a completed handshake). `.authFailed` and `.reconnecting` still land in idle content.

ports_cleanly.capability: Advertise-and-wait waiting-state card (spinner, discoverable-as copy, cancel)
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: ProgressView + "Waiting for your pump" + name-specific or generic discoverable copy; inline error line when fault == .boundElsewhere while the spinner runs; full-width Cancel that stops advertising. All SwiftUI. Two substantive copy changes required by the platform: the advertised name must reflect what iOS actually broadcasts (`CBAdvertisementDataLocalNameKey`), and the card must state that the app has to stay in the foreground with the screen on while waiting, because background advertising is not visible to the pump.

ports_cleanly.capability: Medtronic session timers and GATT service topology
ports_cleanly.ios_approach: 30 s handshake timeout, 60 s FIRST_PAIR pairing-wait window (armed only for first pair; RECONNECT waits indefinitely), and both fault transitions port as plain Swift `Task.sleep` timers on the driver actor. All UUIDs (vendor-base SAKE characteristic, vendor 0x0900 Device Info service, SIG DIS characteristic UUIDs) are expressible as full 128-bit CBUUIDs.

Delivered in background under the `bluetooth-central` background mode. Mirror with `peripheralManagerDidUpdateState` for the advertise-and-wait driver.

ports_cleanly.ios_approach: The Wear module has no pairing UI and the watchOS app must match: no pairing view, no scan list, no code entry, no unpair, and no CBCentralManager instance on the watch. The watch renders forwarded monitoring status only. Connection state reaches the watch as part of the existing forwarded status payload over WatchConnectivity (`updateApplicationContext` for latest-wins state, `transferCurrentComplicationUserInfo` for Smart Stack refresh). Keeping BLE off the watch also avoids watchOS's much tighter background-BLE budget.

`docs/troubleshooting/cant-pair-pump.md` and `docs/daily-use/connecting-medtronic-pump.md` port as content rewrites: drop the Android 11 location-permission prerequisite (iOS needs no location for BLE), drop battery-optimization/Samsung sleeping-apps guidance, and add iOS-specific sections for Settings → Bluetooth → Forget This Device, force-quit-disables-background-monitoring, and Low Power Mode. Fix the documented drift while porting: the shipped UI has one pairing-code field, not two. Both docs must state the fork-and-build TestFlight 90-day rebuild cadence where it affects continuity of monitoring.

needs_redesign.capability: Device identity: MAC address as the pairing/reconnect/storage key

needs_redesign.capability: Tandem connect + authentication state machine (GATT setup sequence)
needs_redesign.why: The Android sequence — `connectGatt(TRANSPORT_LE)` → `refresh()` → `requestConnectionPriority(HIGH)` → `requestMtu(185)` → `discoverServices()` → enable AUTHORIZATION CCCD → auth → enqueue five more CCCDs → 500 ms settle → CONNECTED — contains four steps with no iOS API. Transport selection is implicit (CB is LE-only), cache refresh does not exist (see impossible), connection-priority requests do not exist (the peripheral requests parameters, not the central), and MTU is negotiated automatically at ~185 with `maximumWriteValueLength(for:)` reporting the result. CCCD writes become `setNotifyValue(true, for:)`.
options: Port the sequence minus the four unavailable steps and keep the ordering and settle delay.
Restructure around async/await with `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` per GATT step.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Implement the driver as a Swift actor exposing `connect(identity:code:) async throws`, wrapping each CB delegate callback in a continuation so the ordering (authorization CCCD first, auth, then the remaining five subscriptions) is expressed as straight-line code. Preserve verbatim: the `code.count <= 10` JPAKE-vs-legacy-V1 branch, JPAKE CONFIRMATION when a saved derived secret exists else 5-round BOOTSTRAP, the 30 s AUTH_TIMEOUT_MS, the POST_AUTH_SETTLE_MS = 500 delay before `.connected`, the guard that only promotes to `.connected` if still `.authenticating`, immediate `.authFailed` when no code is available, and clearing saved JPAKE credentials on a round-3/round-4 failure. Assert the negotiated MTU is >= the protocol's minimum and fail loudly if not, since you can no longer request it.

needs_redesign.capability: Tandem reconnect policy (two-phase indefinite backoff)
needs_redesign.why: The FAST phase (10 attempts, 1/2/4/8/16/32 s capped) then SLOW phase (passive autoConnect GATT + 120 s retries, forever) exists to work around Android's lack of a durable pending connection. iOS provides that primitive natively: `connect(peripheral)` with no timeout is a kernel-serviced pending connection that costs the app nothing, survives backgrounding, and — with state restoration — survives app termination and device reboot. Reimplementing the backoff on top of it would be strictly worse: more radio churn, more wakeups, no benefit.
options: Port the two-phase schedule literally on top of connect/cancel cycles.
Replace both phases with a single permanent pending connect, retried only on hard errors.
Hybrid: pending connect plus a low-frequency watchdog rescan.
needs_redesign.recommendation: Replace both phases with one permanent pending `connect(peripheral)` re-armed on every `didDisconnectPeripheral` and on `centralManagerDidUpdateState == .poweredOn`, with no attempt cap and no give-up condition. This preserves the load-bearing safety property — "the pump is a medical device; if the user hasn't explicitly unpaired, always try to reconnect" — and strengthens it. Keep `.reconnecting` as the reported state whenever a pending connect is outstanding and the app is not connected. Keep the counters for diagnostics only, as Android does with `consecutiveReconnectFailures`. Explicitly forbid any give-up-after-N logic in code review.

needs_redesign.capability: Medtronic advertise-and-wait connection state machine (peripheral-role lifecycle)
needs_redesign.why: The state machine itself is portable, but its earliest input is not. Android's `onCentralConnected` fires on a GATT-server connection-state callback and is what cancels the pairing-wait timer, clears the fault, stops advertising, and moves SCANNING/CONNECTING/RECONNECTING → CONNECTING. CBPeripheralManager has no did-connect callback at all: the first observable signal that a central attached is a read/write/subscribe (`peripheralManager(_:didReceiveRead:)` for the Device Info service, or `didSubscribeTo` for SAKE). Keep the deliberate asymmetry that deactivating a driver calls disconnect and not shutdown, so re-enabling reconnects without re-pairing. Keep `reconnectIfPaired()` as a no-op when nothing is paired.

needs_redesign.why: Android has two unpair entry points with materially different effects: the pairing screen does a full teardown (driver unpair, credential clear, OS bond removal, foreground service stop) while Settings clears credentials only, leaving a live BLE session, a running service, and a stale OS bond. This is a latent safety defect on Android and would be worse on iOS, where an orphaned pending connection persists in the OS and the bond can never be removed by the app at all.

Remove one entry point.
Keep both but require confirmation on each.

Both entry points invoke it. Add the Settings confirmation dialog copy to the pairing screen too — Android's pairing-screen Unpair acts immediately on a mis-tap, which on iOS costs a manual Settings trip to recover.

The load-bearing runtime behaviours are the single-instance mutual exclusion and the no-default-activation rule.

Swift Package trait / build-flag gating per driver plus a runtime selector.

Preserve exactly: no default activation on a fresh install, mutually-exclusive single-instance selection with the new driver enabled before the old one is disabled (the slot is never empty), and disabling calls the old driver's disconnect. Preserve the consequence that with no driver selected there is no pump card and therefore no route to pairing — but add an ios_requirement to make that state discoverable rather than a dead end.
